**Do not annotate overlapping mentions** - **Example**: The phrase “von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease” is annotated as **one single disease mention** (Specific Disease category).
Distributed modifiers that each form a disease with the shared head are Composite (e.g., “adenomatous polyps of the colon and rectum,” Example 17).
**Composite Mention**. The coordinated sites each form a disease with the shared head “polyps” (Section 2).
**Label as Specific Disease** when the phrase is anchored to one individuated condition, either: - by a proper name, eponym, acronym, gene, or pathogen identity

Complete, separately headed disease names that each stand alone as mentions (e.g., “Wilms tumor, mesothelioma, leukemias, and breast cancer,” Example 8) remain separate mentions, because splitting them loses no information.
Each listed conjunct carries its own head noun and stands alone as a mention, so they are separate mentions and not a Composite Mention (Section 2).
